subject: Request: Limited SLO tolerance for QuantFlow pilot (multi-region)
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver Rios <oliver.rios@quantflow.com>
Cc: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: QuantFlow pilot kickoff + SLO discussion

Hi Oliver —

Thanks again for agreeing to the 8-week pilot. We attached a draft SOW and a short latency profile we ran against your sample traffic. Two operational items to flag before we kick off:

- Our hosted multi-region configuration will route traffic to a nearest-region pool; because QuantFlow will be testing a model variant with larger context windows, we anticipate a higher tail latency for certain sequences (95th–99th percentile).
- For pilots we typically keep standard uptime SLO at 99.95% and standard service credit terms, but given the experimental multi-region pattern you described, we wanted to ask whether you can accept a temporary, limited SLO tolerance for the pilot window: 99.9% uptime (measured monthly) and a capped monthly service credit of 5% of monthly invoice for any qualifying breach.

This would be a time-bound concession to help us ship the pilot faster while we optimize kv-cache and batching heuristics for your workload. If that’s acceptable we’ll route an executive approval request through Deal Desk for signoff and update the SOW.

Attachments: quantflow_sow_draft_v1.pdf, latency_analysis.csv

Next steps: Oliver — can you confirm with procurement/legal if a temporary tolerance and capped credit are acceptable? Marissa / Avery — I’ll need a greenlight from Deal Desk + your exec signoff if QuantFlow agrees.

Best,
Ben
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Oliver Rios <oliver.rios@quantflow.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Maya Singh <maya.singh@quantflow.com>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: QuantFlow pilot kickoff + SLO discussion

Ben —

Appreciate the clarity and the data. Quick response from our side: procurement is okay with a temporary adjustment but legal (copied) needs the service credit cap in writing and a rollback clause to standard SLOs after the pilot. Two asks from our counsel:

1) A firm rollback date (pilot end + 14 days) to revert to 99.95% SLO unless both parties agree to extend.
2) A single measurable incident methodology clause (how you compute eligibility for credits; we prefer timestamps and per-region buckets).

If you can put those two items in a short clause we can sign off quickly. Otherwise, we may require a higher cap on credits.

Oliver
Head of Procurement, QuantFlow
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 08:33:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: QuantFlow pilot kickoff + SLO discussion

Avery / Ben — forwarding the ask from QuantFlow. Legal wants the rollback window and a clear computation method. Deal Desk prefers to limit permanent precedent risk by making this explicitly time-bound and non-precedential.

My recommendation for the exec approval packet:
- Approve temporary SLO tolerance: 99.9% for pilot months only (May 2027 pilot start through June 2027 pilot end).
- Cap service credit at 5% of monthly invoice; if QuantFlow pushes back require 7% cap as compromise.
- Add explicit rollback clause: automatic revert to 99.95% SLO 14 days after pilot end unless both parties sign an extension; any extension requires finance signoff.
- Add incident eligibility: credits calculated per-region per-calendar-day; an incident qualifies when availability < threshold for region for ≥15 continuous minutes.

I can assemble a one-page executive summary for you, Avery, to route to the CRO and Deal Desk approvers. Need your call: greenlight 5% cap or push to 7% for quicker counterparty acceptance?

— Marissa
Director, Deal Desk Operations
From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 15 May 2027 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: QuantFlow pilot kickoff + SLO discussion

Thanks team — good summary. I’m inclined to approve the 5% capped credit with the explicit rollback and incident definition, provided Finance signs off on the commercial impact (Ben, please confirm expected ARR impact and pilot billing cadence). Rationale: this is a short pilot, low ARR, and a narrower SLO aligns with the increased engineering scope.

Marissa — please prepare the executive packet (one-page ask + suggested wording for the contract clause). Ben — share the expected monthly invoice and any upsell timing so Finance can evaluate. I’ll route to the CRO and mark as high-priority escalation for a same-week signoff.

Avery Johnson
VP, Commercial (Acting)
Redwood Inference
